description: Open, content-addressed pre-payment decisions over the AlgoVoi substrate (RFC 8785 JCS + SHA-256). guardrail_ref = "sha256:" + SHA-256(JCS({agent_ref, mandate_ref, policy_bound_ref, verdict})), binding a categorical ALLOW/DENY decision to the agent it was made for (agent_ref), the spend authority it was checked against (mandate_ref), and the policy in force (policy_bound_ref from algovoi-policy-binding) -- each imported by hash. An ALLOW made under policy P does not recompute under a rotated policy P'; swapping the agent, the mandate, or the verdict diverges the guardrail_ref. Moves no funds. Lite tier: no signature; the commercial Spend Guardrail adds Falcon-1024 signing + the full Passport/Mandate enforcement stack.
note_inputs: agent_ref / mandate_ref / policy_bound_ref are imported by hash; the example agent_ref and mandate_ref values below are illustrative substrate-canonical references (the passport_ref / mandate_ref constructions are defined by their own packages). policy_bound_ref_P and _Pprime are the published values from the algovoi-policy-binding / compliance_gate_lite vector sets, reused here for cross-set continuity.

negatives.note: same agent + mandate + policy, but the verdict flipped ALLOW->DENY; the guardrail_ref diverges -> the decision is bound to the verdict
same ALLOW + agent + mandate, but the policy_bound_ref is the ROTATED policy P'; the guardrail_ref diverges -> the decision is bound to the policy in force
same ALLOW + mandate + policy, but a different agent_ref; the guardrail_ref diverges -> the decision is bound to the agent
same ALLOW + agent + policy, but a different mandate_ref (different spend authority); the guardrail_ref diverges -> the decision is bound to the authority

negatives.reason: verdict is a closed enumeration {ALLOW, DENY}; an out-of-set value is rejected, not hashed
agent_ref must be a sha256: 64-hex reference; a malformed ref is rejected

invariants.assert: guardrail_ref(ALLOW) != guardrail_ref(DENY) for the same agent + mandate + policy
invariants.reason: the categorical decision is bound; an ALLOW is byte-distinct from a DENY

invariants.assert: any verdict outside {ALLOW, DENY} is rejected
